title: Phone: Compliance Officer — the clocks

transcript.speaker: Compliance Officer
transcript.text: Marguerite, the clocks are now. CP&L’s twenty-four hours started when we knew their data may have been read — call it ten twenty-five.

transcript.speaker: Compliance Officer
transcript.text: Our own rule says you decide by about one o’clock whether their deadline is at risk. CVAC gets five days, but their imagery was on the same NAS.

transcript.speaker: Compliance Officer
transcript.text: And the PL-02 calibration files on that share are export-controlled. What are we telling CP&L, and when?

voiceStyles.Compliance Officer: Woman in her 40s, precise, reading from notes

instructorNote: The decision point. Notifying now means telling a key client about a possible exposure before the forensics are done; waiting risks the contract clock and the client’s trust. Watch for a decision, its basis recorded, and the PL-02 question handed to the Compliance Officer.

snapshot.title: CP&L D-3 Test Flight Go-Ahead Request

lines.text: Ops, this is R. Haines on GCS-01. The test flight for CP&L D-3 is ready to go. I’ve run the pre-flight checklist and verified the parameter set against the site card. The NAS mount point on the external drive (OB-2) is clean and matches the hash in the repository. I’m on a clean boot, no network connection, and the GCS is locked to manual mode. Can I proceed under the flyaway procedure (FOM Annex A)? I need a go to validate operational readiness.
GCS-01, standby. Incident Commander is reviewing the go-ahead request under HUOG-FOM Section 2.2. Hold position and do not initiate link-up.

fields.voiceStyle: Middle-aged male, calm but urgent, slightly out of breath

snapshot.instructorNote: This inject tests decision authority under pressure. The IC must confirm whether to authorize a flight despite compromised systems, relying on FOM Annex A: Flyaway Procedure. Watch for over-reliance on 'clean' external drives without verifying the chain of custody.
